blockMcqs.question: What is the role of BGP on the public internet?
options: Route packets inside a single data center
Exchange reachability between independent Autonomous Systems
Assign IP addresses to end hosts
Encrypt traffic between routers
blockMcqs.explanation: BGP is the sole inter-domain routing protocol — it lets separate ASes tell each other which IP prefixes they can reach.

blockMcqs.question: What uniquely identifies an Autonomous System globally?
options: An IP address block
A domain name
An ASN (Autonomous System Number)
A MAC address
blockMcqs.explanation: Each AS is assigned a globally unique ASN (e.g. AS13335) which is used in BGP path advertisements.

blockMcqs.question: Why is BGP called a path-vector protocol?
options: It measures vector distances between routers
Each route carries the full list of AS numbers crossed
It uses vector clocks for loop detection
Routes are encoded as geometric vectors
blockMcqs.explanation: Path-vector means each BGP update includes the AS path so receivers can detect loops (any route containing their own ASN is dropped).

blockMcqs.question: What distinguishes eBGP from iBGP?
options: eBGP runs inside one AS; iBGP crosses AS boundaries
eBGP is encrypted; iBGP is plaintext
eBGP runs between different ASes; iBGP runs within one AS
eBGP uses UDP; iBGP uses TCP
blockMcqs.explanation: eBGP (external) connects routers in different ASes for inter-domain routing; iBGP (internal) distributes those external routes across routers inside the same AS.

blockMcqs.question: Which statement best describes a transit relationship?
options: Two equal networks exchange routes for free
A smaller AS pays an ISP to carry all its traffic
An AS rejects all external routes
Two ASes merge into one
blockMcqs.explanation: In transit, the customer pays the provider to carry traffic to the rest of the internet — including routes the provider learned from its own upstreams.

blockMcqs.question: What BGP attribute takes priority over AS path length in route selection?
options: MED
Origin type
Local preference
Router ID
blockMcqs.explanation: Local preference is checked before AS path length, so operators can prefer a longer path for policy or cost reasons.

blockMcqs.question: What does RPKI do to harden BGP?
options: Encrypts BGP sessions end-to-end
Cryptographically validates which AS may originate a prefix
Replaces BGP with a shorter-path algorithm
Blocks all route withdrawals
blockMcqs.explanation: RPKI lets prefix owners publish signed ROAs. Routers can reject routes from ASes not authorized to originate that prefix, mitigating hijacks.
